Confirm the material specification

State the exact alloy or polymer grade and condition, with the applicable standard. Include the certificates and traceability records required. If substitutes may be considered, identify them for approval and confirm the material documents in the quotation.

Describe the part function and mating assembly. Include loads and operating temperature, with exposure or electrical requirements where relevant. Specify any cleanliness, chemical-contact or ESD limits and the evidence needed for acceptance. If the grade is undecided, send these conditions for engineering review..

Compare materials against the part requirements

The catalog groups parts as aluminum, stainless steel, copper and brass, and engineering plastics. The grades below are examples for selection, rather than a stock list. Properties depend on the grade and condition. Suitability and availability are confirmed for the part and proposed finish in the quotation.

Aluminum
Brochure examples

6061, 7075, 2024

Selection questions

Compare strength, stiffness, part mass, environment and finish needs. Specify the exact alloy and temper.

Stainless steel
Brochure examples

304, 316, 17-4PH

Selection questions

Compare the service environment and mechanical requirements. Specify the grade, condition and any required heat treatment.

Brochure examples

Selection questions

Brochure examples

Selection questions

Selection questions

Provide the exact material designation and intended use for engineering review.

Confirm the alloy designation

The original brochure names C3600 and H62, while the supplied material sheet lists C36000 brass. Their equivalence is not established. Confirm the exact designation and applicable standard in your inquiry.

Define the finish and acceptance criteria

Finishing options depend on the material. Services include deburring and polishing, with blasting, anodizing, passivation or plating where suitable. The quotation confirms the treatment and supporting documents for your part.

Process specification: identify the material and treatment, including the finish standard and revision where applicable. Specify controlled color, gloss, texture, coating thickness or roughness; separate visual appearance from the finish's function.
Faces and edges: mark cosmetic faces and specify edge breaks and deburring or polishing requirements. For bead blasting, agree the appearance and whether a reference sample is needed.
Masking and function: mark protected threads, mating bores and other interfaces, plus surfaces for corrosion protection, electrical contact or sealing. For anodizing, confirm the alloy, color and coating requirements. For passivation or plating, confirm the process specification and protected areas.
Dimensions and inspection: state whether acceptance dimensions apply before or after treatment. Critical dimensions are checked at the agreed stage, including after finishing where required.
Order records: specify the material and treatment documents and acceptance records required. We link the requested documents to the relevant part or batch reference.
